questions.question: The Alagh Committee (1979) set India's poverty line on the basis of:
questions.rationale: The first official poverty line used per-capita calorie norms — 2,400 kcal rural and 2,100 kcal urban per day.

questions.question: Which committee most recently revised India's consumption-based poverty line, recommending about ₹972 (rural) and ₹1,407 (urban) per month?
questions.rationale: The Rangarajan Committee (2014) set higher monthly per-capita spending norms than the earlier Tendulkar line.

questions.question: Based on the Tendulkar methodology, India's poverty ratio:
options: Fell from about 45% in 1993-94 to about 22% in 2011-12
questions.rationale: Fast growth cut the poverty ratio roughly in half over those two decades — about 27 crore people exiting poverty.

questions.question: The Multidimensional Poverty Index uses which three dimensions?
questions.rationale: The UNDP–OPHI MPI measures nutrition, child mortality, schooling, attendance, and six living-standard indicators — deprivations, not income.

questions.question: A Gini coefficient of 0 indicates:
questions.rationale: The Gini runs from 0 (everyone receives an equal share) to 1 (a single person receives everything), summarising the Lorenz curve's sag.

questions.question: MGNREGA, enacted in 2005, guarantees:
options: A monthly income to every citizen
100 days of wage employment per rural household
questions.rationale: The Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act is a legal right to 100 days of paid work per rural household each year.

questions.question: The National Food Security Act (2013) entitles about two-thirds of India's population to:
questions.rationale: NFSA creates a right to subsidised food grains covering roughly two-thirds of the population — the food leg of the anti-poverty architecture.

questions.question: An old weaver cannot find work after mills automate. This is:
questions.rationale: Structural unemployment is a skills mismatch — jobs exist but the worker's skills no longer fit them.

questions.question: Five family members cultivate a small farm that two could manage with no loss of output. This is:
questions.rationale: In disguised unemployment, extra workers' marginal product is near zero — they appear employed but add almost nothing; migration loses nothing.

questions.question: In India's labour statistics, 'Usual Status' measures activity with reference to:
options: Each day of the past week
questions.rationale: Usual Status uses a one-year reference period, capturing the long-term picture; Current Weekly Status uses the past week.
